clue.text: — to all puzzlers

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank: the missing words complete the seasonal greeting a setter sends to solvers at the end of December

explanation.definitionFit: The festive wish said to everyone in late December fills the dash, making a greeting from the setter to all solvers.

clue.text: Myosotis hopes to be so?

parts.note: Myosotis is the botanical name of the forget-me-not, whose name asks to be remembered

explanation.walkthrough: The forget-me-not's name is a plea not to be forgotten, so it hopes to be worth recalling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth recalling is what a flower named 'forget-me-not' wants to be.

clue.text: Cash in hand, waiting for the "go"

definitions.meaning: '... money' or 'the readies' is cash available now
prepared and poised for the starting signal

explanation.definitionFit: Available money is one sense, and prepared to start is the other.

clue.text: Singing style of the true love of "Mistress mine"?

definitions.text: Singing style of the true love of "Mistress mine"?

parts.words: Singing style of the true love of "Mistress mine"?
parts.note: in Twelfth Night's song O Mistress Mine, the true love 'can sing both high and low'

explanation.walkthrough: Feste's song in Twelfth Night says 'your true love's coming, that can sing both high and low'; a style that leaps between high and low notes is the Alpine one.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing that jumps between a chest voice and falsetto, as Alpine herders do, covers both high and low.

clue.text: See 1
Garage, empty ? Put in seed

definitions.meaning: an empty garage is one whose motor is out, gone
an aromatic seed used in baking, as in seed cake

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: the motor is gone, so the garage is empty. 'Put in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A spice seed used in rye bread is one sense; split in two it says the motor is out, so the garage stands empty.

clue.text: Blackmore's John and Leslie make presentations of claret

parts.note: John Ridd is the hero of R. D. Blackmore's novel Lorna Doone
Les is the short form of Leslie

explanation.surface: Two men named John and Leslie hand round glasses of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is slang for blood: to pepper someone with shot draws blood, so it puts claret on show.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce with many holes, as with bullets, makes blood appear, and claret is old boxing slang for blood.

clue.text: One's stocking up in expectation of his arrival

definitions.text: One's stocking up in expectation of his arrival

parts.words: One's stocking up in expectation of his arrival
parts.note: children hang up a stocking on Christmas Eve awaiting the gift-bringer

explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking up' looks like laying in supplies, but it is hanging a stocking up for the Christmas visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded gift-bringer of Christmas Eve is awaited with hung-up stockings.

clue.text: In the pit an old form of musical instrument

definitions.text: In the pit an old form of musical instrument

parts.words: In the pit an old form of musical instrument
parts.note: the orchestra pit holds instruments; an older spelling, with a final E, of a lute-like plucked instrument

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the old spelling of the small round-backed plucked instrument, as played in the orchestra pit.
explanation.definitionFit: This older spelling names the small lute-like instrument with paired metal strings.

clue.text: No nutcracker, with this course (however homophonous) -

definitions.text: No nutcracker, with this course (however homophonous)

parts.words: No nutcracker, with this course (however homophonous)
parts.note: a dessert course needs no nutcracker, and Tchaikovsky's Nutcracker Suite sounds the same, hence 'however homophonous'

explanation.walkthrough: Tchaikovsky's ballet music is the Nutcracker Suite, which sounds the same; the course that comes after the main is a different thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The pudding course of a meal shares its sound with the suite of ballet music.

clue.text: What Alph did for five miles

definitions.text: What Alph did for five miles

parts.words: What Alph did for five miles
parts.note: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan, which runs 'five miles' with a mazy motion

explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's Kubla Khan: 'Five miles meandering with a mazy motion / Through wood and dale the sacred river ran.' The clue asks what that river did.
explanation.definitionFit: A river winding in loops along its course is said to wander or snake, which is what the poem's river does.

clue.text: French veto set back the City for the time being

parts.note: non is French for no, a refusal

indicators.note: set back means the letters for the City are turned round to run in reverse

parts.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London

explanation.surface: A French refusal delays the City's plans for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns EC into CE. The phrase 'for the nonce' means for the time being, so the definition is that whole phrase's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word means the present occasion, as in the idiom 'for the nonce', meaning temporarily.

clue.text: Last month's peripatetic event

parts.note: peripatetic means walking about; the event was the Queen's first informal stroll among crowds, on her 1970 tour of Australia and New Zealand

explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's habit of strolling among crowds to chat, rather than staying in a car, was new in 1970 and got its name from an Australian word for a journey on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's informal stroll to meet ordinary people in the street is a walking event, hence peripatetic.

clue.text: See 11
Witty soul

parts.note: recalls Polonius in Hamlet: the quality that is 'the soul of wit'

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's Polonius says this quality 'is the soul of wit', so it is the witty soul. 'Witty soul' looks like a description of a person, a funny fellow, but it points at the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortness of speech is, by Shakespeare's line, the essence or soul of cleverness in words.

clue.text: Sandy helps in the kitchen

parts.note: sandy describes devices filled with sand that time the boiling of breakfast food

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandy' looks like a person's name, but it means full of sand: small hourglasses timing a boil.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hourglasses time boiling in the kitchen, and their sand makes them sandy helpers.

clue.text: False argument confounds the ship's MO

indicators.note: confounds means throws into confusion, so the following letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, with its S kept as a letter
taken as written, MO being a medical officer

explanation.surface: A bogus line of reasoning baffles the vessel's medical officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounds' scrambles SHIPSMO into the answer; the 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a clever but misleading piece of reasoning, a fallacy dressed to look valid.

clue.text: Like a robber portrayed in disguise

indicators.note: in disguise means the letters of portrayed appear in a changed form

explanation.surface: A thief is depicted wearing a disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disguise' rearranges PORTRAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber lives by plunder and preying on others, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Make monkeys out of us? They may have had the opposite effect

definitions.text: Make monkeys out of us? They may have had the opposite effect

parts.words: Make monkeys out of us? They may have had the opposite effect
parts.note: in evolution, genetic changes turned ape ancestors into humans, the reverse of making monkeys of people

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make monkeys out of' usually means to fool someone; here it is taken literally, and evolution ran the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetic changes across generations are what evolution credits with turning apes into people.

clue.text: Numbers of girls may be, when given rings

definitions.text: Numbers of girls may be, when given rings

parts.words: Numbers of girls may be, when given rings
parts.note: two readings: girls' telephone numbers may be busy when rung, and girls themselves are betrothed when given rings

explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' works twice: phone calls and betrothal rings; 'Numbers' are telephone numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both busy, of a phone line, and promised in marriage, of a person given a ring.

clue.text: In the turn of a card His Majesty makes money

indicators.note: in means the royal letters go inside the turned card
the turn of means the words a card are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A king makes a fortune when a card is turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the turn of' makes DRACA from A CARD, and 'In' puts HM inside it. 'makes' is a link. This was the Greek currency.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the currency of Greece before the euro, and of ancient Greece too.

clue.text: 4 ac this time

definitions.meaning: with the answer to 4 across in front, this gives the gift received at the festive season
the time now, as opposed to past or future

explanation.definitionFit: A gift is one sense, and now, the current moment, is the other.

clue.text: Assumed (an attitude about it)

indicators.note: about means the first word's letters go round the word it

parts.note: to take up an attitude or stance is to strike a pose, so this phrase means posed

explanation.surface: Someone took up a stance on the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: POSED, assumed an attitude, goes 'about' IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward something as a basis for argument is to take it as given, to suppose it.

clue.text: Going round. Irish island, trims the boats

indicators.note: going round means the word trims surrounds the island's letters

parts.note: taken as written
Aran is an island group off the west coast of Ireland

explanation.surface: A sailor circling an island off Ireland adjusts the sails of the boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trims' looks like the verb of sail adjustment, but here it is the outer word; 'Going round' wraps it about the Aran Islands, off Galway in western Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sailing vessels with three hulls side by side.

clue.text: Bound to be recorded

explanation.definitionFit: Fastened with adhesive strip is one sense; captured on a cassette is the other.

clue.text: Confuse learned cleric in drink

indicators.note: in means the cleric's letters sit inside the drink

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a learned clergyman's degree

explanation.surface: A scholarly priest gets muddled by a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'learned' reads as a past-tense verb, but it is the adjective, pronounced learn-ed, describing a Doctor of Divinity; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To muddle or befuddle the mind is the verb's sense, as with a 'muddled' or befuddled head.

clue.text: Check your balance when taking this ale?

definitions.meaning: an inspection of accounts, checking that the books balance
a strong ale once brewed at Oxford and Cambridge colleges for the day the accounts were examined

explanation.walkthrough: 'balance' suggests steadiness after drinking, but it is a bank balance. The second half refers to audit ale, a strong beer of the colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of financial records is one sense; the other names a special strong college beer.

clue.text: Errant naiad?

indicators.note: errant means wandering, so the letters of naiad stray into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Errant' rearranges NAIAD into the Roman goddess of the hunt, who roamed the woods with her nymphs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman huntress goddess roamed forests attended by nymphs, a wandering figure akin to a water sprite.

clue.text: Make earnest appeal for soft graphite

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
the 'lead' in a pencil is graphite

explanation.surface: Someone begs for a gentle grade of pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or entreat strongly is the verb's sense, as in begging a judge for mercy.

clue.text: Lancashire course — Wild Oat coming last causes controversial issue.

indicators.note: coming last means the scrambled oat goes at the end, after the stew

parts.note: Lancashire hotpot is a lamb and potato stew from north-west England, a main course

indicators.note: wild means the letters of oat run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A meal from Lancashire, with wild oats served at the end, sparks argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a race or golf course, but it is a meal's course: the stew. 'Wild' scrambles the grain into ATO, and 'causes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue so contentious that nobody wants to handle it is called this, like something too hot to hold.

clue.text: Ignore 24's crazy red rag

parts.note: 24 down names a goddess, whose short form Di gives Di's

indicators.note: crazy means the letters of red rag are jumbled

explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' turns RED RAG into REGARD. The answer to 24 down shortens to DI, and with the possessive gives DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay no heed to something, to leave it unnoticed, is a synonym.

clue.text: He wrote poems of the old, old army girls

parts.note: ye is an old form of the, as in 'ye olde shoppe'
the ATS, Auxiliary Territorial Service, was the women's branch of the British Army in the Second World War

explanation.surface: A poet writing verse about elderly former servicewomen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. Irish poet W. B. Yeats.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet, Nobel laureate, author of The Second Coming.
